trades.holding_period_note: sessions_held is measured per closed tranche of an average-cost lot, so tranches of the same lot share its entry date and their intervals overlap; they must not be summed. sessions_in_market is the union.

costs.note_price_difference: slippage_bps / price_difference is measured against the decision mid and therefore INCLUDES intraday drift (it can be negative). execution_cost_bps is friction only.

implementation_shortfall.note: drift is the mid's own movement between decision and execution; it is a timing outcome, not a fee, and is reported separately from the friction components.

pnl_decomposition.note: Realized and open P&L are net of explicit cash costs (commission, exchange and regulatory fees less rebates), which are the only costs charged to cash separately; spread, depth and impact are already inside the fill prices. The residual is the rounding gap and is reported rather than hidden.

narrative.headline: Beat the market: +26.22% total return vs +14.41% for the index, +6.96pp residual after beta, -14.3% max drawdown, 0.06% of capital lost to execution costs.

clauses.text: Finished at +26.22% against the S&P 500's +14.41% over the same 251 sessions - an excess return of +11.81pp.
The beta premium this participant is built to harvest was live (+35.95% over the season) and the account made money - a tailwind that cannot be separated from skill on one path.
The low_vol premium went against the declared exposure (-29.73% for a +0.5 loading) yet the account still returned +26.22% - the result was driven by something other than this factor.
Of the +26.22% total, about +19.26pp is explained by carrying beta 1.34 against a +14.41% market (R^2 0.93); the residual +6.96pp is everything else - selection, timing, leverage and cost.
SPY contributed +24,429 USD (93% of net P&L) across 33 closed trades; SPY was the biggest drag at +24,429 USD.
Execution cost 63 USD (0.06% of starting capital, 0.2 bp per fill, 0.2 bp of the 3,000,582 USD traded). 50% of that was spread/depth/impact and 50% was explicit fees and rebates.
33 closed round trips, 63.6% winners, profit factor 8.29, average winner +1,323 vs average loser -279 USD, median holding 133 sessions.

Time in market, measured without double counting: 251 sessions held at least one position (the per-tranche holding periods above sum to 4225 sessions because tranches of the same average-cost lot share its entry date, so they overlap and must not be added together).
Single worst trade: SPY long 2025-09-17 to 2026-04-06, -1,634 USD.
Worst peak-to-trough drawdown -14.26% (-9.10% for the index), trough on 2026-03-30, recovered 2026-04-14. Average gross exposure 139% of starting capital, peak leverage 2.04x.
Daily returns were +0.31 skewed with excess kurtosis +3.22; historical 95% VaR -1.76%/day with CVaR -2.51%/day. Worst single session -3.47%, best +5.84%.

prose.title: Mandate (as declared before the season)
prose.text: @VIXRegime_Timer (VIX Regime Timer) ran the "volatility regime timing" archetype. Declared thesis: This participant trades the one genuinely real exogenous series in Season 1: the daily CBOE VIX close from FRED. Equity returns cluster with volatility regimes, so hold the index ETF at maximum leverage when realised fear is high and the market is falling, and cut leverage when the regime is quiet and extended. Entry: VIX >= 24 and the index is below its 20-session mean: 2.0x long SPY (distress buying); VIX between 18 and 24: 1.5x long SPY; VIX < 18 and the index is above its 20-session mean: 1.0x long SPY; VIX < 15 and 21-session index return > 6%: 0.5x (extended, quiet). Exit: Regime change only; no stop loss. Sizing: leverage set by the regime table. Leverage: 0.5x - 2.0x gross. Cadence: daily, horizon all season. Aggression 3/5. This participant was built to maximise return, not to manage risk: Concentrates the entire account into the index and varies leverage 4x between regimes.
